item.title: [TIFF - Toronto Film Festival] CHRONOVISOR Trailer | TIFF
item.description:
The Chonovisor is a legendary, occult time-viewing device invented by an Italian Benedictine monk in the 1950s, who claimed to have witnessed the crucifixion of Christ through his machine that could visually capture and relay any moment in history through a television set. Chronovisor, the debut feature from filmmakers Kevin Walker and Jack Auen, is a docu-fiction hybrid that follows Béatrice (Anne-Laure Sellier), a respected academic, who risks her reputation as she becomes transfixed by this allegedly true story. Her obsession with researching the mythical machine takes her from her Upper East Side apartment to the hidden depths of New York’s libraries. This mystery has been compared to Umberto Eco’s The Name of the Rose and has been described by film critics as an “academic-noir.” Shot entirely on 16mm in warm low light, the film is also a remarkable formal exercise in scanning and capturing pages, translations, recordings, photographs, drawings, and videotapes. The film had its world premiere at Rotterdam and was selected to screen at New Directors/New Films. This is its Canadian Premiere.

In his final interview on screen, Giorgio Armani reflects on his life and his brand's undeniable influence on Italian fashion and taking America by storm with the wardrobe for Richard Gere in 'American Gigolo' (1980).

Set against Milan’s lavish and exclusive fashion sanctuaries, amidst ateliers, runways, and private retreats, the film explores creative rivalries, personal stories and the enduring love affair between Hollywood and Italian designers.

Featuring insights from fashion icons, actors, industry insiders and collaborators, including Sharon Stone, Tom Ford, Helen Mirren, and Samuel L. item.title: [Palace Films] HOLY CANNOLI - Official HD Trailer - Only In Cinemas
item.description:
http://www.palacefilms.com.au/holy-cannoli © Palace Films

Witty, romantic and smart, the eagerly-awaited new film from beloved Italian satirist Pierfrancesco ‘Pif’ Diliberto ('The Mafia Kills Only In Summer') - adapted from his own bestselling novel - is a hugely entertaining and gently irreverent comedy about love, faith and finding the perfect pastry.

Sicily, present day. Arturo (Pif) is a real estate agent near-infallible at his job, but far less so in love. A creature of habit, Arturo lives alone, is the weak link in his office's five-a-side football team, and nurtures a single, unwavering passion: desserts - the delights and criticisms of which he posts on social media. He especially loves the sciù (Palermo's favourite cream-filled choux buns) from the city's most celebrated pasticceria. His life lights up when he meets the owner’s daughter, the fervently religious Flora (Giusy Buscemi), who's looking to rent a space to open her own patisserie. Falling instantly, hopelessly in love, Arturo is thrust into a world of belief and moral expectation far beyond his comfort zone. To win Flora over, he embellishes his commitment to Catholicism and embarks on an increasingly absurd attempt to live by the gospel, a quest so unlikely it earns him a most unexpected spiritual advisor: the Pope himself.

By turns playful, pointed and cheeky, HOLY CANNOLI channels Pif’s distinctive gift for using comedy to explore the contradictions of contemporary Italian life, in this case as experienced by a soul-searching, sweet-toothed sceptic.

A tender, secret bond slowly grows between these two solitary teens, both hovering between childhood and the adult lives that await them...

item.title: [The Match Factory] Nuestra Tierra | Trailer | Lucrecia Martel
item.description:
In October 2009, Javier Chocobar, a member of the indigenous Chuchagasta community in northwest Argentina’s Tucumán Province, tried to defend himself and his people from being forcibly evicted from their land by a local landowner and two former police officers. As a result, the 68-year-old Chocobar was shot and killed, and two other community members were wounded. In her expansive and enlightening first feature documentary, Argentinean filmmaker Lucrecia Martel (Zama, 2017) takes a sweeping approach to this tragic true story, triangulating the murder trial of the three men, the lives of Chocobar and his fellow Chuchagasta people, and the centuries-old, colonialist legacy of land and property theft across Latin America. With a ravishing, at times vertiginous visual approach to filming the natural beauty of the contested land, Martel pays cinematic tribute to people whom others systematically tried to erase from history.

item.title: [The Match Factory] Below The Clouds | Trailer | Gianfranco Rosi
item.description:
Between Mount Vesuvius and the Gulf of Naples, the ground shakes periodically and the fumaroles of the Phlegraean Fields taint the air. From the traces of history, memories of the subterranean world, and the concerns of the present, in black and white, a lesser-known Naples emerges and fills with voices, with lives. Below the clouds lies a territory crisscrossed by locals, worshippers, tourists, and archaeologists excavating a past that in museums will give new life and meaning to statues, fragments, and ruins. The train that rings Vesuvius makes its rounds as racehorses train along the shore. A teacher runs a makeshift afterschool for children and adolescents. Firemen in their command center calm the fears of the locals who call in, law enforcement tracks down tomb robbers, while in the port of Torre Annunziata, Syrian tankers unload Ukrainian grain. The land that skirts the gulf is a vast time machine.
